# Typical error of each method

Design 9.3 and VAL-5: each method's typical error is measured by leaving one chip out. For every chip that has
a measured value, the method estimates it as if the measurement did not exist, and the estimate is compared
with the measurement. The two parts of the A100 family carry the same measured values, so they are left out
together; otherwise each would predict itself from its twin.

The figures below cover 911 measured points of the committed coefficient registry. A ratio is
`max(estimate/truth, truth/estimate)`: 1.00 is exact and 2.00 is a factor of two either way.

- **Same generation** is the median of the same quantity on the other chips of the held-out chip's architecture
  generation, and gives no estimate for a chip with no sibling. It is the predictor `extrapolate_by_generation.py` writes.
- **Global median** is the median over every other chip. It is the baseline a method must beat.

A family with fewer than 10 held-out points is merged into `other`, and `other` is left out if it too has fewer.
What this does not yet measure: the roofline (rank 6) and vendor-specification (rank 5) methods. Each estimates
a value from a datasheet figure, so measuring its error needs an estimator that reads the chip's datasheet; the
two above read only other chips' measurements. Until such an estimator is written, the page states no error for
those methods and says so rather than reusing the figures above for them. The whole-run error is the dashboard's.
